distillation_scope.leaf_granularity: First-layer toxicologic disease leaf for systemic salicylate poisoning. Acute ingestion, chronic accumulation, delayed absorption, enteric-coated preparations, topical or bismuth salicylate exposure, co-ingestion, and severity strata are represented as mechanisms, axes, risk factors, or treatment modifiers rather than disease-name qualifiers.
distillation_scope.ranking_note: Likelihood should consume exposure evidence, serum salicylate level and trend, mixed acid-base physiology, tachypnea, otologic symptoms, GI symptoms, CNS toxicity, pulmonary edema, renal clearance, glucose status, and treatment-context axes when observed.

latent_mechanisms.display_name_ja: サリチル酸曝露・吸収負荷
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Systemic salicylate load from ingestion, chronic therapeutic accumulation, delayed gastric emptying, bezoar or enteric-coated absorption, topical absorption, or salicylate-containing preparations. This upstream burden drives serum concentration and supplies ongoing input to downstream toxicity.
Salicylate directly stimulates the medullary respiratory center, producing tachypnea, hyperventilation, low PaCO2, and an early respiratory alkalosis that may coexist with metabolic acidosis.

latent_mechanisms.display_name_ja: ミトコンドリア酸化的リン酸化脱共役
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Salicylate uncouples oxidative phosphorylation, increasing heat production and oxygen demand while reducing ATP generation, driving hyperthermia, lactate production, ketosis, and organ stress.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Organic acid accumulation and high anion gap acidosis
latent_mechanisms.display_name_ja: 有機酸蓄積・高アニオンギャップ性アシドーシス
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Lactate, ketoacids, salicylic acid, renal hypoperfusion, and impaired clearance lower bicarbonate and raise the anion gap. The acidemia component may emerge late in acute toxicity or dominate chronic toxicity.

latent_mechanisms.display_name_ja: アシデミアによる組織内トラッピング
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Lower blood pH shifts salicylate toward the nonionized form, increasing CNS and tissue penetration. This creates a feed-forward loop where falling pH worsens neurologic toxicity even when serum concentration is not extremely high.

latent_mechanisms.display_name_ja: 中枢神経サリチル酸毒性
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Direct CNS salicylate exposure, energy failure, acidemia, and glucose dysregulation produce tinnitus, agitation, delirium, coma, seizures, and cerebral edema risk.

latent_mechanisms.display_name: Volume depletion and renal salicylate clearance failure
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Vomiting, diaphoresis, fever, poor intake, and salicylate renal effects reduce effective circulating volume and glomerular filtration. Impaired renal clearance sustains salicylate burden and makes urinary alkalinization less effective.

Severe salicylate toxicity can increase pulmonary capillary permeability and produce noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, hypoxemia, and acute respiratory failure, sometimes worsened by volume loading or chronic toxicity.

latent_mechanisms.display_name_ja: 血小板・凝固機能障害
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Cyclooxygenase inhibition, platelet dysfunction, gastric mucosal injury, and in severe cases coagulation disturbance increase bleeding tendency, especially in patients taking antithrombotics or with gastrointestinal injury.

latent_mechanisms.display_name_ja: 血糖異常・神経糖欠乏
latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Increased cerebral glucose consumption and altered systemic glucose balance can produce hypoglycemia or CNS neuroglycopenia despite normal measured serum glucose, amplifying altered mental status and seizures.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Systemic absorbed salicylate is reflected by measured serum salicylate concentration, with delayed or rising levels when absorption continues.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: More likely with delayed absorption, enteric-coated preparations, bezoar physiology, or insufficient decontamination.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Continuing gastrointestinal absorption can make serial salicylate levels rise or rebound after an initial measurement.
Salicylate irritates the gastrointestinal tract and stimulates nausea.
Vomiting is a common early manifestation and contributes to volume depletion.
Medullary stimulation causes tachypnea and hyperventilation.
The clinical counterpart of respiratory center stimulation is rapid breathing, often out of proportion to pulmonary findings early.
Hyperventilation lowers PaCO2 and produces a respiratory alkalosis component.
Early respiratory alkalosis can raise pH before metabolic acidosis predominates.
Uncoupled oxidative metabolism generates heat and can produce fever or hyperthermia.
Energy failure and increased anaerobic metabolism raise lactate.
Altered metabolism and fasting physiology can increase ketone production.
High heat production and agitation can progress to dangerous hyperthermia.
Uncoupling increases lactate and ketoacid generation, feeding the high anion gap acidosis.
Accumulation of lactate, ketoacids, and salicylate raises the anion gap.
Severe salicylate poisoning produces clinically apparent high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis from organic acid accumulation and impaired clearance.
The intensity of organic acid burden tracks the severity of bicarbonate depletion and acidemia.
Organic acid buffering consumes bicarbonate.
When metabolic acid generation outstrips respiratory compensation, systemic pH falls.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Active when arterial or systemic pH is low.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Acidemia increases the nonionized salicylate fraction and tissue penetration.
Greater nonionized salicylate penetration into CNS increases neurotoxicity.
Tinnitus is a classic otologic manifestation of salicylate toxicity.
Auditory disturbance may include reversible hearing loss or muffled hearing.
CNS salicylate burden, acidemia, and energy failure cause confusion, delirium, or coma.
Severe CNS salicylate penetration and energy failure can progress from agitation or delirium to coma and absent airway protection.
Seizures are an observed manifestation of severe CNS salicylate toxicity, especially with acidemia or neuroglycopenia.
Severe CNS toxicity can progress to seizures or status epilepticus.
Severe poisoning can produce cerebral edema, especially when acidemia and energy failure are present.
Systemic hypoglycemia may occur, while CNS glucose deficit can be clinically important even with normal serum glucose.
Neuroglycopenia is inferred when CNS toxicity is disproportionate to measured serum glucose or improves with dextrose support.
CNS glucose deficit amplifies delirium, coma, and seizure tendency.
Vomiting, diaphoresis, fever, and poor intake make volume depletion clinically visible.
Reduced renal perfusion or intrinsic kidney injury raises creatinine and impairs salicylate elimination.
Volume depletion and kidney injury reduce urine output, limiting renal salicylate clearance.
Sustained hypovolemia and salicylate toxicity increase AKI risk.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Most relevant with severe acidemia, established kidney failure, anuria, or dialysis dependence; uncomplicated salicylate toxicity more often has low or normal potassium.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Renal clearance failure and acidemia can produce clinically important hyperkalemia during severe salicylate poisoning.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Active when renal filtration, urine flow, or urine alkalinization is inadequate.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Reduced renal clearance sustains systemic salicylate burden after absorption.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Adequate potassium facilitates urinary alkalinization; hypokalemia makes alkalinization difficult.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Hypokalemia promotes renal hydrogen secretion and impairs the ability to alkalinize urine.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Active when urine pH is alkaline and urine flow is adequate.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Ion trapping in alkaline urine increases salicylate renal elimination.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Active when pH is maintained in an alkalemic or non-acidemic range.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Higher blood pH reduces nonionized salicylate fraction and CNS penetration.
Pulmonary edema causes shortness of breath and increased work of breathing.
Alveolar edema impairs oxygenation.
The mechanism becomes visible as noncardiogenic pulmonary edema on exam, imaging, or oxygenation.
Pulmonary edema and fatigue can progress to respiratory failure.
Pulmonary edema, respiratory muscle fatigue, or loss of compensatory hyperventilation can make respiratory failure clinically present.
Severe pulmonary edema, coma, or fatigue can progress to assisted ventilation or intubation in salicylate poisoning.
Marked hyperkalemia can produce QRS widening in severe poisoning or renal failure contexts.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Most relevant when potassium is markedly elevated or QRS widening is present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Severe hyperkalemia and acidemia can precipitate malignant ventricular arrhythmias.
Severe permeability edema can meet ARDS-like physiology.
Cyclooxygenase inhibition impairs platelet aggregation even when platelet count is not low.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: More likely with severe toxicity, hepatic stress, coagulopathy, anticoagulants, or vitamin K deficiency.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Severe poisoning or comorbid anticoagulation can produce measurable coagulation abnormality.
Gastric mucosal irritation plus platelet dysfunction can cause hematemesis, melena, or occult bleeding.
Bleeding hazard rises when platelet dysfunction intersects with mucosal injury, anticoagulation, trauma, or severe coagulopathy.
AKI reduces clearance and worsens acid-base control, increasing death risk.
Cerebral edema is a major terminal pathway in severe salicylate toxicity.
Seizures worsen acidosis, hyperthermia, aspiration risk, and CNS injury.
Failure to maintain ventilation and oxygenation can rapidly worsen acidemia and tissue salicylate distribution.
Refractory acidemia accelerates tissue trapping and cardiovascular/CNS collapse.
Severe hyperthermia increases metabolic demand, rhabdomyolysis risk, and neurologic injury.
Salicylate exposure can irritate gastric mucosa and present as epigastric discomfort.

axes.shape_free_text: Observed or strongly inferred exposure to salicylate-containing substances. Route, timing, dose, formulation, and chronic accumulation are child axes.
Dose and exposure intensity proxy integrating amount, concentration, duration, chronicity, formulation, and repeated dosing.

axes.display_name_ja: 急性高用量サリチル酸内服
axes.shape_free_text: A short-window high-dose oral ingestion context; this is an exposure pattern, not a disease-name qualifier.

axes.display_name_ja: 慢性サリチル酸蓄積コンテキスト
axes.shape_free_text: Repeated therapeutic or supratherapeutic salicylate use with accumulation; clinical toxicity can occur at lower measured levels than in isolated acute ingestion.
axes.clinical_interpretation: Route/subtype context for salicylate poisoning. It should explain the case when present, but absence of this alternative exposure route must not be treated as evidence against salicylate toxicity.

axes.display_name_ja: 外用・ビスマス系サリチル酸曝露
axes.shape_free_text: Non-classic salicylate source such as topical preparations, methyl salicylate, or bismuth subsalicylate-containing products.
axes.clinical_interpretation: Route/subtype context for salicylate poisoning. It should explain the case when present, but absence of this alternative exposure route must not be treated as evidence against salicylate toxicity.

axes.display_name_ja: 腸溶・吸収遅延コンテキスト
axes.shape_free_text: Enteric-coated tablets, bezoar physiology, pylorospasm, delayed gastric emptying, or persistent gastrointestinal reservoir.
Estimated salicylate dose normalized by body weight when history, pill count, or product concentration allows calculation.

axes.display_name_ja: サリチル酸曝露からの時間
axes.shape_free_text: Time from last meaningful salicylate exposure or ingestion to clinical assessment or sampling.

axes.display_name_ja: 併用中毒・混合過量内服
axes.shape_free_text: Co-ingested sedative, acetaminophen, alcohol, anticholinergic, or other toxic exposure that can mask salicylate physiology or add independent hazards.
Measured serum salicylate concentration. Interpretation depends on timing, chronicity, pH, renal function, and clinical toxicity.

axes.display_name_ja: 血清サリチル酸再上昇・上昇傾向
axes.shape_free_text: Serial salicylate levels rise, fail to fall as expected, or rebound after an initial decline.

axes.display_name_ja: 呼吸性アルカローシス・代謝性アシドーシス混合所見
axes.shape_free_text: Acid-base pattern combining low PaCO2 with low bicarbonate and elevated anion gap, with pH variable by phase and severity.
Presence of metabolic acidosis, typically high-anion-gap physiology from salicylate, lactate, ketoacids, renal impairment, or loss of respiratory compensation.

axes.display_name_ja: 代謝性アシドーシス重症度
axes.shape_free_text: Severity of metabolic acidosis from bicarbonate depletion, high anion gap, and low systemic pH.
Measured arterial or venous pH interpreted with respiratory and metabolic components; acidemia greatly increases salicylate tissue penetration.
Arterial carbon dioxide tension; typically low from salicylate-induced hyperventilation unless respiratory fatigue, sedative co-ingestion, or ventilation failure occurs.
Serum bicarbonate decreases from metabolic acidosis and compensation; also directly affected by bicarbonate therapy.

axes.display_name_ja: 血清アニオンギャップ
axes.shape_free_text: Anion gap rises from lactate, ketoacids, salicylate, and renal impairment.
Lactate reflects mitochondrial uncoupling, tissue stress, seizures, hypoperfusion, and coexisting shock.
Urine pH determines renal ion trapping of salicylate and is a treatment-response axis during alkalinization.
Potassium is often low from alkalosis, vomiting, and renal losses, but severe acidemia or renal failure can produce dangerous hyperkalemia; hypokalemia impairs urinary alkalinization.
Clinically relevant hyperkalemia in severe salicylate poisoning, especially with marked acidemia, renal failure, or dialysis dependence.
Measured serum glucose; low or low-normal values may be clinically important because CNS glucose deficit can occur even when serum glucose is not profoundly low.
Ketosis or ketone positivity contributing to high anion gap physiology.
Patient-reported nausea in the toxicologic presentation.
Vomiting as a parent finding; severity and dehydration are represented separately.
Frequency, persistence, or clinical consequence of vomiting.
Abdominal pain from gastric irritation, vomiting, or coexisting pathology.
Intensity or functional impact of abdominal pain.
Tinnitus or ringing in the ears associated with salicylate effect.
Reduced hearing or muffled hearing during salicylate toxicity.
Sweating from sympathetic activation, hyperthermia, or illness stress.
Clinical volume depletion from vomiting, diaphoresis, fever, poor intake, or osmotic/renal losses.
Degree of volume depletion based on orthostasis, mucous membranes, urine output, weight loss, or perfusion.
Rapid breathing or hyperventilation, especially when early and disproportionate to lung findings.
Measured respiratory rate.
Measured body temperature; salicylate toxicity can produce hyperthermia from uncoupled metabolism, agitation, or seizures.
Measured heart rate, often elevated with dehydration, fever, agitation, pain, or hypoxemia.
Perfusion pressure; may fall with dehydration, severe acidemia, shock, or co-ingestion.
Pulse oximetry or oxygen saturation; may fall with pulmonary edema, aspiration, ARDS-like physiology, or respiratory failure.
Subjective shortness of breath or clinically noted breathing discomfort.
Any altered mental status including confusion, agitation, delirium, somnolence, coma, or poor arousal.

axes.display_name_ja: 意識・精神状態異常重症度
axes.shape_free_text: Severity of altered mental status, from mild confusion or agitation to coma, unresponsiveness, and loss of airway protection.
Agitation, delirium, restlessness, hallucination, or unsafe hyperactive mental status.
Depressed consciousness, somnolence, stupor, or coma.
Observed seizure activity in the clinical course.

axes.display_name_ja: 神経糖欠乏コンテキスト
axes.shape_free_text: Clinical context suggesting CNS glucose deficit, such as altered mental status or seizures with low, low-normal, or rapidly falling glucose.
Measured serum creatinine reflecting kidney function and salicylate clearance capacity.
Blood urea nitrogen; rises with dehydration, kidney dysfunction, or gastrointestinal bleeding.
Urine output; low values indicate poor renal clearance capacity and limit urinary alkalinization.
Coagulation measurement; severe toxicity, liver stress, anticoagulants, or bleeding context can raise INR.
Platelet functional inhibition inferred from salicylate exposure, platelet function testing, mucosal bleeding, or antiplatelet effect.
Hematemesis, melena, hematochezia, occult blood loss, or clinically suspected salicylate-associated gastrointestinal bleeding.
Clinical or radiographic pulmonary edema not primarily explained by cardiogenic volume overload.
Bilateral airspace or interstitial opacities compatible with pulmonary edema or ARDS-like physiology.
Radiographic or clinical extent of pulmonary edema.
Clinical respiratory failure in severe salicylate poisoning, including failure of compensatory ventilation, pulmonary edema, apnea, or need for ventilatory support.
Severity of respiratory failure, including ventilatory fatigue, apnea, intubation, mechanical ventilation, or severe hypoxemia.

axes.display_name_ja: 重炭酸ナトリウム治療コンテキスト
axes.shape_free_text: Context in which alkalinization is being considered or delivered: salicylate toxicity with acid-base disturbance, renal clearance goal, or urine alkalinization target.

axes.display_name_ja: アルカリ化実施可能性
axes.shape_free_text: Adequate vascular access, potassium repletion, urine flow, monitoring capacity, and absence of prohibitive fluid overload for bicarbonate-based alkalinization.

axes.display_name_ja: 体液過剰・肺水腫コンテキスト
axes.shape_free_text: Context where fluid or bicarbonate volume may worsen pulmonary edema or oxygenation.

axes.display_name_ja: 血液透析アクセス可能性
axes.shape_free_text: Availability of dialysis-capable access, anticoagulation plan, hemodynamic tolerance, and extracorporeal clearance resources.
Need for airway protection from coma, severe agitation, aspiration risk, or respiratory failure.
Risk that sedation, paralysis, or insufficient minute ventilation after intubation will abruptly raise PaCO2, lower pH, and worsen tissue salicylate trapping.
Hazard of AKI from hypovolemia, toxicity, or comorbidity, with salicylate clearance implications.

axes.display_name_ja: 難治性アシデミアハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Hazard of persistent or worsening systemic acidemia despite ventilation, bicarbonate, volume, and clearance efforts.
Hazard of cerebral edema from severe CNS salicylate toxicity, acidemia, or energy failure.

axes.display_name_ja: けいれん・てんかん重積ハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Hazard of seizures or status epilepticus during CNS salicylate toxicity.

axes.display_name_ja: 急性呼吸不全ハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Hazard of respiratory failure from pulmonary edema, fatigue, aspiration, or loss of compensatory hyperventilation.
Hazard of ARDS-like acute hypoxemic respiratory failure from permeability edema or aspiration.
Hazard from dangerous hyperthermia and metabolic acceleration.
Hazard of clinically important bleeding from platelet dysfunction, gastrointestinal injury, anticoagulants, or severe coagulopathy.

axes.display_name_ja: サリチル酸中毒死亡ハザード
axes.shape_free_text: Lifespan outcome hazard emerging from refractory acidemia, CNS toxicity, cerebral edema, respiratory failure, AKI, hyperthermia, pulmonary edema, seizures, and delayed clearance.
Aspirin or aspirin-containing product as the salicylate source; formulation-specific details are child satellites.
Enteric-coated aspirin exposure, which can delay absorption, prolong salicylate levels, or contribute to pharmacobezoar behavior.
Methyl salicylate source such as oil of wintergreen or topical salicylate products.
Oral ingestion of methyl salicylate, a high-concentration salicylate exposure route.
Reported or estimated salicylate mass ingested, when body weight is unavailable for mg/kg normalization.
Ventricular tachycardia or malignant ventricular rhythm during severe salicylate poisoning, usually mediated by severe acidemia, hyperkalemia, hypoxemia, or underlying cardiac substrate.
Burden and severity of ventricular tachycardia, from brief runs to sustained unstable ventricular tachycardia.
QRS widening in the context of severe hyperkalemia or metabolic poisoning physiology; not specific to salicylate but relevant to severe presentations.

axes.clinical_interpretation: Epigastric discomfort or pain is a reusable satellite of abdominal pain from gastric irritation, including salicylate overdose.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Higher salicylate burden tends to co-vary with high anion gap physiology, though timing and chronicity create exceptions.
Respiratory alkalosis couples low PaCO2 with higher pH early; later metabolic acidosis can override this relationship.
Loss of bicarbonate buffer contributes directly to systemic acidemia.
Falling pH defines acidemia severity and increases the hazard of refractory acid-base failure.
Alkaline urine increases ion trapping and renal elimination of salicylate when urine flow is adequate.
Hypokalemia makes urine alkalinization difficult, so potassium and urine pH move together during treatment response.
Renal dysfunction reduces clearance and sustains serum salicylate concentration.
Pulmonary edema increases the risk of oxygenation failure and ventilatory collapse.
Severe altered mental status increases aspiration and airway-protection needs.
Observed seizure activity is direct evidence that recurrent or sustained seizure hazard is high.
Active gastrointestinal bleeding increases near-term major bleeding hazard, especially with platelet dysfunction or anticoagulants.
Refractory acidemia is a direct near-term death pathway through CNS trapping, cardiovascular instability, and respiratory failure.
Cerebral edema is a high-lethality complication in severe salicylate poisoning.
Respiratory failure removes compensatory hyperventilation and can rapidly worsen salicylate distribution and hypoxemia.

treatments.display_name_ja: 曝露中止・サリチル酸源除去

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Exposure termination only has causal effect when ongoing or repeat salicylate input exists.
Stopping repeated dosing removes the persistent input term sustaining toxicity.

treatments.context_specific_role: Stops the upstream toxin input so clearance and antidotal supportive vector fields can dominate.

treatments.display_name_ja: 活性炭単回または反復投与

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Benefit decreases as unabsorbed gastrointestinal salicylate disappears, though delayed absorption can preserve benefit.
Delayed absorption or persistent tablets provide ongoing luminal toxin that charcoal can bind.
Aspiration risk can block or delay enteral charcoal unless the airway is protected.

side_effects.interpretation: Charcoal can worsen nausea or vomiting.
Aspiration risk matters when mental status is impaired or vomiting is uncontrolled.

treatments.context_specific_role: Reduces ongoing gastrointestinal absorption when timing or delayed absorption leaves salicylate in the gut.

treatments.display_name_ja: 静注重炭酸ナトリウムによる血液・尿アルカリ化

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Correcting acidemia reduces nonionized salicylate and tissue trapping.
Hypokalemia prevents effective urine alkalinization unless potassium is repleted.
Low urine flow limits renal salicylate elimination even if urine pH rises.
Bicarbonate infusion volume or sodium load may worsen pulmonary edema.

side_effects.interpretation: Alkalinization can lower potassium and impair its own urine-pH effect if not replaced.
Sodium and fluid load may worsen pulmonary edema or fluid overload.

treatments.context_specific_role: Raises serum and urine pH to reduce tissue trapping and enhance renal salicylate elimination.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Correction is most beneficial when hypokalemia is blocking urinary alkalinization.
Oliguria or severe renal impairment increases hyperkalemia risk and reduces alkalinization effect.

side_effects.interpretation: Over-repletion can cause hyperkalemia, especially when renal function is poor.

treatments.context_specific_role: Enables urinary alkalinization and corrects arrhythmia-relevant electrolyte disturbance.

treatments.display_name_ja: 等張晶質液による循環血液量補正

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Restoring volume improves renal salicylate clearance and perfusion when depleted.
Fluid can worsen pulmonary edema or oxygenation if permeability edema is present.

side_effects.interpretation: Excess volume can worsen pulmonary edema or oxygen requirement.

treatments.context_specific_role: Restores perfusion and urine flow needed for renal elimination and bicarbonate therapy.

treatments.display_name_ja: 神経糖欠乏に対するブドウ糖補正

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: CNS symptoms with low or low-normal glucose increase the expected benefit of dextrose.
Marked hyperglycemia reduces need for additional glucose except in special contexts.

side_effects.interpretation: Dextrose can cause hyperglycemia if continued without monitoring.

treatments.context_specific_role: Offsets CNS glucose deficit that can amplify altered mental status and seizures.

treatments.display_name_ja: けいれん・高度興奮に対するベンゾジアゼピン

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Active seizure is the direct target of anticonvulsant effect.
Respiratory suppression or rising PaCO2 can worsen acidemia in salicylate toxicity.

side_effects.interpretation: Sedation can reduce compensatory hyperventilation and raise PaCO2.

treatments.context_specific_role: Controls seizure and dangerous agitation while preserving ventilation monitoring as a salicylate-specific safety constraint.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Cooling directly targets dangerous hyperthermia.
Ongoing seizures generate heat and require simultaneous seizure control.

treatments.context_specific_role: Lowers heat burden while definitive salicylate clearance and acid-base control proceed.

treatments.display_name_ja: 過換気維持を伴う気管挿管・人工換気

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Airway control is most useful when coma, aspiration, or respiratory failure creates an airway emergency.
Failure to maintain pre-intubation minute ventilation can abruptly raise PaCO2 and worsen acidemia.
Controlled ventilation can reduce PaCO2 when respiratory failure has already emerged.

side_effects.interpretation: Induction and ventilation mismatch can worsen salicylate tissue trapping if PaCO2 rises.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rescue airway vector field that must preserve compensatory hyperventilation physiology while oxygenation and clearance are addressed.

treatments.display_name_ja: 高効率血液透析・体外除去

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Extracorporeal clearance directly removes salicylate, so higher burden increases absolute benefit.
CNS toxicity indicates dangerous tissue penetration and benefit from rapid clearance plus pH correction.
Dialysis corrects acidemia and removes salicylate when bicarbonate alone is insufficient.
Access and dialysis availability determine how quickly the clearance vector can start.

side_effects.interpretation: Extracorporeal therapy can cause hypotension in unstable patients.
Vascular access and anticoagulation can increase bleeding hazard in selected contexts.

treatments.context_specific_role: Rapidly removes salicylate and corrects acid-base failure when endogenous clearance and alkalinization are insufficient.

high.trajectory_modulation: Chronic accumulation and severe toxicity can occur at lower serum concentrations, with higher pulmonary edema, renal clearance failure, and mortality hazards.

present.trajectory_modulation: Reduced renal salicylate clearance sustains serum concentration, weakens urinary alkalinization when urine flow is low, and increases dialysis relevance.

axis_response_modulation.conditionality: especially when acidemic or dialysis dependent
especially when acidemic or dialysis dependent

present.trajectory_modulation: Volume depletion reduces renal clearance and amplifies tachycardia, AKI hazard, and acid-base instability.
Serum levels can rise late or rebound, prolonging absorption and requiring serial levels and decontamination context.
Co-ingestion may blunt compensatory hyperventilation, mask tinnitus or tachypnea, and accelerate acidemia and tissue trapping.
Maternal acid-base and salicylate burden can affect fetal exposure; maternal physiology and fetal risk make pH control and clearance context more consequential.
Bleeding event hazards increase when salicylate platelet effects intersect with anticoagulants, antiplatelet drugs, or baseline coagulopathy.
More time for acidemia, tissue trapping, renal failure, pulmonary edema, and CNS toxicity to accumulate before treatment.

risk_factors.clinical_rationale: Massive aspirin/salicylate ingestion strongly supports salicylate toxicity and raises acute exposure burden, level, acid-base, and GI-irritation axes.
Massive aspirin/salicylate ingestion strongly supports salicylate toxicity and raises acute exposure burden, level, acid-base, and GI-irritation axes.
Enteric-coated aspirin or pharmacobezoar context prolongs absorption and makes delayed or persistent salicylate levels plausible.

supportive_care: Serial salicylate concentrations until clearly falling with clinical improvement.
Serial blood gas, electrolytes, anion gap, glucose, renal function, urine pH, and urine output monitoring.
Continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring and frequent neurologic reassessment.
Avoid sedative-induced loss of compensatory hyperventilation unless airway and minute ventilation are actively controlled.
Treat vomiting, maintain potassium and volume status, and monitor for pulmonary edema during alkalinization.
Early toxicology, nephrology, and critical care coordination when CNS toxicity, acidemia, renal failure, pulmonary edema, or rising levels are present.

Exactly one derived_hazard axis is present: mortality_hazard_in_D-SALICYLATE-TOXICITY.
Acute, chronic, delayed-absorption, and formulation contexts are represented as axes and risk/context modifiers, not disease-name qualifiers.
